desc:
Ecommerce order and returns reports turn your order data into answers you can read in minutes. Ecom Swift LLC builds clear weekly or monthly reports on orders, returns and delivery times in a sheet or dashboard that you own.

## What is an order report?

An order report is a summary of what your store sold and what happened afterwards. It counts orders, shows which products sell, tracks returns and refunds, and measures how long delivery takes. A good report answers a question and points to a next step.

Your store admin already shows some of this data. The problem is that it is scattered across screens and exports, and few owners have time to join it together every week.

## Why data you do not read does not help

Without a regular report, decisions rely on memory and mood. A slow week feels like a crisis, a busy day feels like growth, and a rising return rate goes unnoticed until it drains profit. Reports replace that guessing with a consistent view you can compare from one period to the next.

A report is also a record. When a carrier performs badly or a product starts to come back often, you want dated evidence you can show a supplier or a partner.

## How reporting improves decisions

Reports work because they put related facts side by side. Orders by product show what to restock. Returns by reason show whether the cause is sizing, quality or description. Delivery time by carrier and region shows where promises are broken, and fulfilment delay views show where orders get stuck before they ship.

Each of these ties to action: reorder, fix a product page, switch a service, change a promise at checkout. Repeat order views also show whether customers come back, which tells you if your effort should go to new buyers or existing ones.

## What a useful order report set includes

- Orders, sales and average order value for each period.
- The best-selling products and those that rarely sell.
- Returns and refunds, grouped by reason.
- Delivery time by carrier and by destination region.
- Orders that took long to ship after payment.
- Repeat purchase view showing returning customers.
- Weekly or monthly refresh that needs no manual work.
- Plain-language notes next to each figure.
- A short list of what stands out and what to examine next.

## What we do

We begin by asking which decisions you want the reports to support. We then pull the order data from your store, clean it and build the reports in the place that suits you: your store's own reporting, a spreadsheet or a dashboard. You own the file and the account, so the reports stay with you.

We set the refresh schedule and check that each figure matches the source. Then we explain each report in simple words, so you understand how a number is calculated and what it can and cannot tell you. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many reports, how much history and how much commentary we include, up to a dashboard with a first monthly write-up and a call.

Reports describe the past and the pattern. They cannot promise a result, and external factors like season and promotions can change the numbers.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide a few questions first, then look for the data.
- Compare the same periods, such as month with month.
- Record any big promotion or stock-out next to the numbers.
- Review the report on a fixed day each week or month.
- Act on one finding at a time.

**Avoid:**
- Tracking dozens of measures that nobody reads.
- Mixing test orders with real ones.
- Comparing a holiday week with a quiet week.
- Treating a single odd day as a trend.
- Sharing customer details in a report meant for staff.

## Who this is for

This suits an owner who wants to know which products to reorder and which to drop. It suits a store with a rising number of returns and no clear reason. It also suits a business preparing to talk to an investor, a supplier or a new manager, which needs trusted numbers.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you want to learn and where your orders live. We need view access as a staff or collaborator user, and we usually only need order totals, product names, dates and statuses. We do not need customer personal details for most reports. We never need passwords. Send any existing sheets and we will build on them.
